title: Multivariate Analysis Reveals Phenotypic Groups Among Peruvian Maize Races
content: Maize (Zea mays L.) in Peru exhibits extensive phenotypic diversity traditionally classified into races based on morphological characteristics, but quantitative relationships among races remain insufficiently known. In the present analysis, morphological data from 43 Peruvian maize races were analyzed using principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering to identify discriminant descriptors and phenotypic groups. From 68 quantitative descriptors retained after data completeness filtering, nine non-redundant variables associated with leaf, tassel, and ear morphology captured the main patterns of phenotypic variation. The first two principal dimensions explained 77.50% of the total variation, with leaf and tassel traits predominating in the first dimension and ear characteristics in the second. Hierarchical clustering separated the races into four phenotypically differentiated groups characterized by distinct combinations of leaf, tassel, ear, and cob–rachis traits. These groups showed only partial correspondence with the historical racial classification, indicating that quantitative phenotypic similarity represents an additional dimension of maize diversity. The results provide a parsimonious quantitative basis for characterizing Peruvian maize germplasm and support the complementary use of multivariate phenotyping and historical racial classification for conservation and breeding.
